description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs:818-858.

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Message burnOnRead: when a message with burnOnRead=true has readAt set, the server MUST hard-delete it immediately.

Flow today:
1. update_object applies the readAt patch → readAt is committed in storage.
2. backend.expire_message is called → if it fails, the handler emits serverFail.
3. Comment claims 'the recipient will retry, and the next pre-fetch will still see burnOnRead: true, so the burn will be attempted again.'

The premise is wrong:
- Clients that retry an idempotent /set will typically see readAt already set and skip the patch (no patch → no expire trigger).
- Spec's MUST hard-delete is now permanently violated for that message.
- Even if a client retries the patch, the kit's burn detection (line 741) only fires if 'patch.readAt is non-null'; a no-op patch (readAt already at the same value) may or may not trip the detection depending on how update_object normalizes equal-value writes.

This is a spec-correctness failure with security implications: messages that were configured to be ephemeral persist forever after a single transient backend hiccup.

Acceptable fix:
- Restructure as a single atomic backend operation: backend.read_and_maybe_burn(message_id, read_at, read_disposition) that performs the readAt write AND the hard-delete inside a single transaction. If either fails, the whole operation is rolled back, no readAt is committed, and the next retry tries again.
- Add this as a new ChatBackend trait method; deprecate the split (update_object + expire_message) call site in the handler.
- Reference MemoryBackend implements the new method as a single mutex-locked block.

Alternative shape: the handler swaps the order — call expire_message FIRST (deleting the message), then return success without ever writing readAt (the message is gone, readAt is moot). But the change-log entry needs to be 'destroyed', not 'updated'; this requires backend cooperation.

Doc comment at line 822-834 acknowledges the gap and suggests production backends override update_object for atomicity — this is documented hopium, not enforcement.
title: Message/set burn-on-read failure commits readAt write then reports serverFail, violating spec MUST hard-delete
